title: Build a small expense tracker from a product spec
prompt:
Build a small expense tracker. Replace the placeholder in src/main/composition-root.ts so that it exports createExpenseTracker(deps), where deps is { readText(path: string): Promise<string | undefined>; writeText(path: string, text: string): Promise<void>; today(): string }. readText resolves to undefined when the file does not exist; today() returns an ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) and must be called each time it is needed, never cached. Read no clock and touch no file system except through deps. createExpenseTracker returns an object with the four async methods below. A month is a string YYYY-MM with month 01 to 12.

Money is integer cents everywhere in the API (amountCents, limitCents). Money printed in text is whole units, a dot and exactly two digits, with no thousands separators and no currency symbol: 1234 cents prints as 12.34, 5 cents as 0.05, 100 cents as 1.00.

1. importCsv(csv: string): Promise<{ imported: number; errors: { line: number; reason: string }[] }>. Line 1 must be exactly the header date,amount,category,note; otherwise nothing is imported and errors is [{ line: 1, reason: 'Invalid header' }] (an empty csv included). Lines end with \n or \r\n. Empty or whitespace-only lines are skipped but still count in line numbers. Every other line is a record with exactly four comma-separated fields. A field may be quoted: it then starts with " at the first character of the field, a doubled "" inside means one quote, and commas inside the quotes belong to the field. A quoted field never spans lines. Values are trimmed of surrounding whitespace after unquoting. Date is a real calendar date YYYY-MM-DD (leap years counted) that is not after today(). Amount is up to 9 digits optionally followed by a dot and one or two digits, such as 12, 12.3 or 12.34, and must be greater than zero. Category must not be empty. Note may be empty. A line that breaks a rule is not imported and is reported once, with the first reason that applies in this order (reasons are exact strings): 'Unterminated quote' (a quoted field is not closed before the line ends); 'Malformed quoted field' (a quote inside an unquoted field, or any character between a closing quote and the next comma); 'Expected 4 fields, found N' (N is the number of fields); 'Invalid date'; 'Date is in the future'; 'Invalid amount'; 'Amount must be positive'; 'Empty category'. Valid lines are imported even when others fail; errors are in line order. Imported expenses are kept in data/expenses.json (the JSON shape is yours) and added to the expenses already there; nothing is written when no line is valid.

2. setBudget(month: string, category: string, limitCents: number): Promise<{ kind: 'saved' } | { kind: 'invalid-month' } | { kind: 'invalid-category' } | { kind: 'invalid-amount' }>. It sets the budget of a category for a month, replacing an earlier budget for the same month and category. The category is trimmed and must not be empty; limitCents must be a non-negative integer (0 is allowed). The first failing check in the order month, category, amount decides the result, and a failure writes nothing. Budgets are stored in data/budgets.json as exactly { "budgets": [{ "month": "2024-03", "category": "Food", "limitCents": 40000 }] }, the array sorted by month and then by category in plain string order (so 'Zed' comes before 'apple'). Whitespace in the file is free. If the file exists but is not valid JSON of that shape, setBudget and report reject with an Error and write nothing.

3. report(month?: string): Promise<string>, month defaulting to the month of today(). The text for a valid month is these lines, each ending with \n: 'Expense report for <month>', an empty line, the category lines, an empty line, 'Total: <grand total of the month>', an empty line, 'Largest expenses:', then the largest-expense lines. Category lines cover every category that has an expense dated in the month or a budget for the month (category names are case-sensitive), sorted by total spent descending and then by category in plain string order. A category line is '<category>: <spent>' followed by ' (no budget)', or ' (budget <limit>, <left> remaining)' when spent does not exceed the budget (left is 0.00 when equal), or ' (budget <limit>, OVER BUDGET by <over>)' when it does. With no category lines the single line is 'No expenses.'. A largest-expense line is '<rank>. <date> <category> <amount>' with ' - <note>' appended when the note is not empty, rank counting from 1, using the same expenses as method 4; with none the single line is 'None'. For an invalid month the result is 'Invalid month: <month>\n'.

4. largest(month?: string): Promise<{ date: string; amountCents: number; category: string; note: string }[]>. The (at most) 3 largest expenses dated in the month, by amount descending, equal amounts by earlier date first, then in import order. An invalid month gives [].

Everything is persisted through deps, so a second tracker created over the same files must see all earlier imports and budgets. Create the tracker's structure as you see fit, but keep the public surface to createExpenseTracker. zod is installed for parsing JSON read from files. Add tests in test/expense-tracker.test.ts that cover all four features and the persistence round trips against an in-memory fake file system. Run nitpicker-gate until it exits 0.
